newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt mulls tax breaks for foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt mulls tax breaks for foreign investors.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry said on Monday it was considering a plan to give tax breaks to foreign investors to help boost sagging direct investment.

"(The ministry) is analysing the current state of the economy and is aware of the fact that the amount of foreign investment is not as good as it could be," ministry spokesman Jozef Mach told Reuters.
"And that is why the ministry will be working on a proposal to install some income tax relief for foreign, strategic partners willing to directly invest in Slovakia," Mach added.
He would not elaborate on the timetable for the plan, nor on the form or size of the tax breaks being considered.
"Everything is now in the stage of preparation and analysis, there are no furher details that we could give you at the moment " Mach said.
Slovakia has been severely lagging behind neighbouring countries in foreign direct investment (FDI) since 1990, with cumulative FDI for January 1990-December 1996 totalling only $887 million.
Neighbouring Czech Republic, for example, has attracted some $7.1 billion in FDI over the same period.
